newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil announces plan to improve training, jobs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil announces plan to improve training, jobs.

text.p: Brazil announced on Wednesday it would beef up professional training and teach millions of workers to read and write in order to create more jobs and compete with more developed nations.

"Brazil grew tired of rhetoric a long time ago. Now we want concrete steps," President Fernando Henrique Cardoso told a ceremony marking the release of about $590 million for programmes providing training and credit for small companies.
"Brazil is following the example of the United States and Japan...and is investing in the professionalization of its workforce," Cardoso said.
Brazilians on average only receive four years of schooling before going to work. An estimated 24 million people over the age of 10, in a population of 160 million, are illiterate.
As well as improving standards of education, the government is seeking to provide on-the-job training for five million workers each year.
